newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME prices soft in Asia, fail to breach resistance.
newsitem.headline: LME prices soft in Asia, fail to breach resistance.

text.p: London Metal Exchange copper prices were soft in quiet Asian trade on Wednesday after they failed to breach resistance levels earlier, traders said.
"During the morning, copper tried to penetrate resistance at $2,390 but there was no follow-through by users," said a trader at a major trading house.
"The dollar's decline (against the yen) helped induce buying from the Japanese," he said.

Traders said they expect copper as well as aluminium to remain confined to their recent trading ranges later in London, even though some copper selling might emerge in relation to an expiry in options.
While fundamentals for aluminium were strong, the upside was capped on expectations that producers would place sell orders above $1,640, traders said.
On Tuesday, base metals closed steady in London in thin trade, with traders saying the trend was likely to continue.
At 0710 GMT, LME benchmark three-month copper was quoted at $2,352/57 a tonne, up from $2,350/55 at 1800 GMT on Tuesday but down from $2,360 at the Tuesday afternoon kerb close.
Aluminium was quoted at $1,630/32 a tonne, unchanged from $1,632.00 at the close of Tuesday's afternoon kerb.
